name: Radical feminism
summary: Radical feminism holds that male supremacy is the oldest and most basic form of domination, that women form an oppressed sex class, and that patriarchy is built into the family, sexuality, religion, law and culture rather than being a matter of unequal laws alone. It seeks the root transformation of these institutions rather than reform: abolishing sex roles and the patriarchal family, securing women's control over reproduction, and ending men's sexual use of women through rape, pornography and prostitution.
scope: This profile represents the radical feminism of the American women's liberation movement from 1967 (New York Radical Women, Redstockings, The Feminists, Radicalesbians; Firestone, Millett, Hanisch) and its later theoretical and legal development by Andrea Dworkin and Catharine MacKinnon, with Mary Daly and Adrienne Rich as cultural and lesbian-feminist influences, as historicised by Alice Echols. Where these strands split — on pornography law (anti-pornography versus anti-censorship feminists), separatism and political lesbianism, essentialist cultural feminism, reproductive technology and trans inclusion (gender-critical versus trans-inclusive radical feminists) — answers are neutral or low confidence. Socialist, liberal and anarcha-feminism and gender-critical feminism as a distinct current are not covered here.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Radical feminists campaigned for women's control over reproductive health care and grew out of the New Left, so support for guaranteed care is inferred rather than a stated program plank.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Millett and the Redstockings Manifesto name women's underpaid wage labor as part of their oppression; support for a higher legal minimum is inferred from that, not a stated demand.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Firestone looked to a post-scarcity cybernetic economy and the movement came from the anticapitalist New Left, so skepticism of market allocation is inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Radical feminist texts treat male supremacy rather than ownership of industry as the root problem and take no position on nationalising utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redstockings pledged to put the interests of the poorest women first, from which a mild preference for progressive taxation is inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Hanisch and Redstockings saw all women as workers and favored collective action, so a favorable view of unions is inferred; the movement itself organised outside unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Millett describes marriage as a financial alliance in which women are treated as property, and Firestone ties class to ownership; a weak view of property rights is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Dworkin and MacKinnon target the profit-making pornography and sex industries for legal liability, which points toward tighter regulation of business generally only by inference.

cut-welfare.rationale: Redstockings defined its interest as that of the poorest, most exploited woman, so cutting support for poor women is inferred to be opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is a socialist-feminist rather than radical feminist concern; radical feminist sources do not take it up.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss counterterror surveillance; mild opposition is inferred from their distrust of male-run state power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug legalisation is not discussed in radical feminist sources; MacKinnon notes addiction among the pressures pushing women into prostitution.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: MacKinnon argues in Only Words that group-directed attacks are discrimination rather than protected speech, but anti-censorship feminists from the same movement opposed such laws, so the answer is low.

strong-leader.rationale: Radical feminist groups rejected leaders and hierarchy as male, using lot systems and leaderless consciousness-raising groups.

state-harmful.rationale: MacKinnon calls the state male, yet radical feminists consistently look to law for abortion access, rape law, civil remedies against pornography and penalties on buyers of sex, so they do not reject the state as such.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Dworkin notes that police are often among the abusers of prostituted women and radical feminists distrust male institutions, so more police power is inferred to be opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: MacKinnon rejects the sex work approach of decriminalising or legalising the sex trade and calls for criminalising buyers and pimps; Dworkin calls prostitution intrinsically abusive.

decide-locally.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not take a view on levels of government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Millett calls the family patriarchy's chief institution and Firestone calls for breaking the tyranny of the biological family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Radical feminists supported lesbian lives but many rejected marriage as an institution, so support for extending it is mild and inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: New York Radical Women held abortion-repeal rallies, and Dworkin says the feminist goal was decriminalised abortion grounded in a woman's absolute control of her body.

more-religion-public.rationale: Millett and Firestone treat religion as a source of patriarchal ideology, so a larger public role for it is rejected.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Redstockings pledged to repudiate racial privilege and to put the poorest women first, and the movement grew from civil rights work.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Millett argues that sex differences in temperament are cultural rather than biological and that psychosexual personality is learned after birth.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Radical feminists treat inherited culture as patriarchal, so preserving national traditions is inferred to be opposed.

gradual-change.rationale: Radical feminists rejected gradual reform: Daly says equal-rights reforms leave patriarchy intact and the Redstockings Manifesto ends 'this time we are going all the way'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International organisations are not discussed in the classic radical feminist sources.

free-trade.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not take up trade policy.

nation-first.rationale: Radical feminists see women as an international class, so national interest is inferred to be secondary.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military intervention is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

limit-growth.rationale: Growth limits are not addressed; ecofeminist strands near Daly differ from Firestone's technology-driven abundance.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy postdates the classic texts and radical feminist sources give no position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Firestone hoped technology would free women from reproduction, while radical-cultural feminists feared it would entrench male control; adherents are split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not discussed in the radical feminist sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Redstockings took 'red' for revolution and Firestone called for a feminist revolution against the sex-class system, though in a social rather than insurrectionary sense.

experts-over-public.rationale: Redstockings held women's own experience to be the basis for understanding their condition and distrusted ideologies produced by male culture.

central-planning.rationale: Apart from Firestone's cybernetic utopia, radical feminist texts are silent on planned versus market economies.

socialized-markets.rationale: Radical feminist sources give no view on market socialism; economic form is secondary to sex-class in their analysis.

land-value-tax.rationale: Radical feminist writing does not discuss land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is not discussed in radical feminist texts, which focus on women's legal and sexual subordination.

basic-income.rationale: Economic dependence on men is, for Millett, a main source of women's subordination, so an unconditional income that ends that dependence is inferred to be welcome.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection is not a radical feminist topic.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Radical feminist texts do not address the distribution of property among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Firestone imagined labor itself abolished through cybernetics, but most radical feminists did not take up the abolition of money; the answer is neutral and low.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary policy is outside radical feminist concerns.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised corporate bodies of employers and workers would be male-run hierarchies of the kind Millett says patriarchy builds; opposition is inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Radical feminists rejected the vanguard politics of the male left and organised in leaderless groups, so single-party rule is inferred to be rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is the patriarchal principle in its purest form for Millett's analysis of rule by fathers; rejection is inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Radical feminists practised internal democracy but saw existing democracies as male-dominated, so support is mild and inferred.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' councils are a socialist concern radical feminists did not take up.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

natural-rulers.rationale: Millett rejects biological justifications for male rule, and radical feminists rejected leaders within their own groups.

political-violence-never.rationale: Radical feminist sources neither endorse nor rule out political violence; Dworkin wrote about resistance to male violence but the movement used nonviolent protest.

war-builds-character.rationale: Radical feminists link aggression and force to the male role Millett describes as conditioned; glorifying war is inferred to be rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: Radical feminists see organised religion as a mainstay of patriarchy and fought church influence on abortion law.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Millett says patriarchy has God on its side and Firestone names Judeo-Christianity as a source of women's inferiority, so scripture-based law is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Radical feminists seek remedies through public law, so privatised courts are inferred to be opposed.

military-superiority.rationale: Radical feminist texts link militarism to male aggression; opposition is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Redstockings pledged to repudiate privileges of race that divide women; ethnic nationhood is inferred to be rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Firestone replaces economic class with a materialist history based on sex, and Redstockings call male supremacy the oldest and most basic domination.

equal-outcomes.rationale: MacKinnon's critique of formal equality and Redstockings' focus on the poorest woman point toward substantive equality, by inference.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Civilisational blocs are not a radical feminist topic.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not state a view on individual self-interest as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Community duty has historically been used to bind women to family roles Millett criticises; opposition is inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Daly's gyn/ecology celebrates natural life, while Firestone wants to overcome nature's constraints on women; there is no common position.

limit-population.rationale: Radical feminists demand women's reproductive control, not population targets; the sources take no view on limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Firestone welcomed technology while cultural feminists like Daly condemned male necrophilic culture; there is no shared view on industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Firestone welcomed reproductive technology but warned it could also reinforce oppression, and radical-cultural feminists opposed it; no common view.

human-enhancement.rationale: Firestone's artificial reproduction is a kind of enhancement, but radical-cultural feminists opposed such technology; no common view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic government is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: Radical feminists treat past social orders as patriarchal; Firestone and Millett describe every historical civilisation as male-dominated.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Radical feminists judged actions by whether they help women, which the Redstockings Manifesto says matters more than labels such as 'revolutionary' or 'reformist'; that is close to judging results but from a firm commitment.

direct-action.rationale: The movement worked through zaps, pickets, speakouts and the 1968 Miss America protest, and Daly rejected equal-rights reforms won through existing institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Radical feminist groups insisted on internal democracy and leaderless structures to avoid reproducing male hierarchy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not advocate a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Firestone says the division of labor would end by eliminating labor through cybernetics, and the sexual division of labor is a core target for radical feminists.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Firestone drew on Engels's vision of a classless society, which implies distribution by need; most radical feminists did not address it.

production-for-use.rationale: Firestone's goal of a cybernetic economy beyond labor implies production for need rather than profit, but this is inferred from one author.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Radical feminists located exploitation primarily in sex-class rather than in profit; the Marxist labor-theory claim is not theirs.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Radical feminists broke with the male left; Firestone warns that revolutions use women and then drop their demands, so working-class dictatorship is inferred to be rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organisation is not a radical feminist topic.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Redstockings Manifesto treats capitalism and imperialism as extensions of male supremacy, not as causes in their own right; no view on this claim follows.

taxation-theft.rationale: Radical feminists look to the state for abortion access, rape law and civil remedies, so the libertarian claim that taxes are theft is inferred to be rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin treat pornography and prostitution as harms to women as a class even where individuals consent, which departs from the liberal harm principle; the inference is low.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Radical feminism analyses women as an oppressed class, and MacKinnon argues that attacks on a group reach each of its members.

conscription.rationale: Radical feminists treat the military as a male institution; opposition to conscription is inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not compare exit and voice.

state-as-business.rationale: Market models of government are foreign to radical feminist thought; mild opposition is inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Millett and Firestone tie women's freedom to escaping economic dependence and reproductive burdens, not only to legal non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not compare media and academic power with elected power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Millett rejects biological explanations of social hierarchy and Redstockings repudiate race privilege; rejection is inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families would rest on the patriarchal family Millett calls patriarchy's chief institution; rejection is inferred.

total-state.rationale: Radical feminists distrust the male state and organised in leaderless groups, so total state control is inferred to be rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: Narratives of national rebirth typically restore family and gender roles that radical feminists reject; opposition is inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Radical feminist texts link conquest and force to the male role; opposition is inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal loyalty is patriarchal rule in a form Millett criticises; rejection is inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Radical feminists compare women's status to slavery and oppose bound labor; rejection is inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: MacKinnon treats objectivity as the male point of view imposed as neutral, and Redstockings regard existing ideologies as products of male supremacist culture.

universal-morality.rationale: Radical feminists make universal claims about women's oppression but distrust reason-based moral systems produced by men; no clear answer.

single-common-good.rationale: Radical feminists see politics as conflict between sex classes, not as reasoning toward a shared good; disagreement is inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is not a radical feminist topic; Dworkin's late Scapegoat supported Israel but this is not a movement position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a radical feminist topic.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workplace democracy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

school-vouchers.rationale: School choice is not a radical feminist topic.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in radical feminist sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: Radical feminist texts do not discuss economic freedom as a condition of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss moral exemplars in government.

national-self-determination.rationale: National self-determination is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

force-without-un.rationale: International law on force is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Radical feminists criticise religion but also ground knowledge in women's felt experience through consciousness-raising rather than abstract reason; no clear answer.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The pledge to put the poorest and most exploited women first suggests opposing exclusion of immigrants from welfare, by inference.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements fall on poor mothers whose unpaid domestic labor Millett and Redstockings already count as exploitation; opposition is inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Radical feminists rejected framing politics around economic classes at all, so the worker-employer question gets no clear answer.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss cultural heritage institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Geopolitical blocs are not a radical feminist topic.

workers-nation.rationale: Radical feminists do not organise around the working class at all.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Millett says sex roles assign women domestic service and men achievement, and the Radicalesbians say sex roles define women as a serving caste; radical feminists reject them.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not discussed in radical feminist texts.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Radical feminism grew partly out of civil rights work and Redstockings pledged to repudiate racial privilege.

state-class-instrument.rationale: MacKinnon treats the state as male rather than as a tool of an economic ruling class; on the statement's economic sense radical feminists take no position.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed in radical feminist sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration policy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy theory belongs to ethnic nationalism, which radical feminists reject; opposition is inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

national-mission.rationale: Radical feminists treat imperialism as an outgrowth of male supremacy, per the Redstockings Manifesto; opposition is inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Redstockings Manifesto calls male supremacy the oldest, most basic form of domination, and Millett says society, like all historical civilisations, is a patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Radical feminists criticise male power rather than political elites as corrupt; no populist position.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Radical feminists insist that reproductive decisions belong to women free from pressure by doctors and governments, so state eugenics is inferred to be opposed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Radical feminists document abuse by police and soldiers of women; support for accountability is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Radical feminists want the state to act against rape, pornography and prostitution, more than a minimal state allows.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Redstockings repudiated racial privilege; opposition is inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Radical feminism demands that women be treated as fully human; the Redstockings Manifesto protests that women's humanity is denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss socialist strategy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not discussed in the classic sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal-status laws disadvantage women, which radical feminists attribute to religion; support for uniform civil law is inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Radical feminists encouraged women to leave patriarchal churches, as in the West German church-exit campaign, so restrictions on leaving or converting are inferred to be opposed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Radical feminists see religion as patriarchal ideology; opposition to religious instruction in state schools is inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Firestone's abortion rally argued that men exclude women from making the laws that govern them, implying authority needs women's consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are outside radical feminist concerns.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts Redstockings' pledge against racial privilege; opposition is inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Radical feminists oppose male force against women but use the state's coercion against pimps and buyers; the libertarian axiom gets no clear answer.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Radical feminists value collective action and sisterhood over competition, as in Hanisch; disagreement is inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Dworkin says women's freedom is diminished by fear of male violence, and radical feminists treat men's power over women as unfreedom even when not exercised.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

vanguard-party.rationale: Radical feminist groups rejected leaders and formal organisation as male, and broke with the vanguard politics of the left.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Redstockings Manifesto states that the movement defines its best interest as that of the poorest, most brutally exploited woman.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The movement used pickets and protest itself, as at the Miss America pageant, so restrictions on picketing are inferred to be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Population and poverty are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Radical feminists sought solidarity across race and class among women; disagreement is inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The Feminists chose media spokeswomen by lot inside the group, but radical feminists made no proposal for public office.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss emergency powers; opposition is inferred from distrust of male state power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not a radical feminist topic.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radical feminists built independent women's presses and rejected party discipline; opposition is inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Military command is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Radical feminists organised without binding party discipline; mild opposition is inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational union is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive powers are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Male episcopal rule is the church patriarchy radical feminists criticise; opposition is inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Radical feminists treat religious authority as a pillar of patriarchy; Millett says patriarchy has God on its side.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Dworkin and MacKinnon frame their pornography law as a civil-rights remedy for harm, not moral censorship, and anti-censorship feminists oppose censorship outright; opposition to virtue-based censorship is inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: Citizen militias are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural versus urban life is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not a radical feminist topic.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Radical feminists criticised male expertise, not education as such; Millett deplores women's exclusion from education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Radical feminists condemn practices such as genital mutilation across cultures as patriarchal, which Daly's Gyn/Ecology did and Lorde criticised; they do not treat cultures as beyond judgement, by inference.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Radical feminists were skeptical of reforms inside male institutions, as Daly's rejection of equal-rights reform shows; no clear view on equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Original appropriation of property is not a radical feminist topic.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: International criminal law is not discussed in the classic sources; MacKinnon later litigated wartime sexual violence internationally.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Millett and Firestone read biblical narratives such as the Fall as patriarchal myth rather than revealed truth.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Radical feminists judge every institution by women's equality, so guaranteed women's participation is inferred to be supported.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defense of planned states is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

indirect-election.rationale: Indirect election is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

national-church-status.rationale: Radical feminists see established churches as patriarchal; opposition is inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Territorial autonomy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Plebiscites are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Colonial borders are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

simple-living.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not advocate or reject simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Radical feminists reject sex-based legal roles but also oppose the military as a male institution; no clear answer.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Spiritual ties to a homeland are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Radical feminists seek legal remedies through courts; killings without trial are inferred to be rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Kin minorities abroad are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Natural-resource ownership is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

self-ownership.rationale: Dworkin bases abortion rights on a woman's absolute control of her body, yet radical feminists reject the idea that selling sexual access is an exercise of ownership, so the libertarian principle gets no clear answer.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not weigh targeted versus universal benefits.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Radical feminists distrusted parties but valued autonomous women's groups, and rejected leaders altogether; no clear answer.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business privileges are not discussed in radical feminist sources.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Denominational politics is not discussed in radical feminist sources.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Radical feminists treat ancestral values as patriarchal, so a return to them is inferred to be rejected.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Radical feminists oppose the husband's legal authority over the wife, which Firestone describes historically as women's civil death on marriage, and treat women's freedom to leave as basic.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource nationalism is not a radical feminist topic.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Radical feminism treats male power over women as structural rather than a matter of fair procedure; it did not discuss distributive theory, so inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; financial regulation is outside its concerns.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Radical feminists placed sex class first but did not deny racism; inferred that they see racism as a continuing obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: MacKinnon and others argue that law embodies male power and lacks legitimate authority over women; the Redstockings-era protests also defied the law, but strands differ.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Firestone argued that cybernation could free people from labour and the sexual division of work; inferred as the view of the wider movement, which did not address it much.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not discussed; nothing in the sources links radical feminism to a view of world power structure.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Radical feminism replaces class with sex class as the basic division; it did not address value theory, so inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Radical feminists regard nation and state as patriarchal institutions; inferred, as patriotism was not a topic of its core texts.

material-over-identity.rationale: The slogan 'the personal is political' makes sexuality, family and culture the core of politics, not secondary to material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its rejection of male-led hierarchies that it would reject one-party communist rule.

missingStatements.text: Prostitution should be ended by criminalising the buying of sex and pimping while decriminalising the people who sell sex.
missingStatements.rationale: MacKinnon calls for criminalising buyers and pimps while decriminalising prostituted people, the Swedish or Nordic model, which defines the radical feminist position on prostitution and is distinct from both prohibition and legalisation.
missingStatements.declined: Statement bank frozen on 2026-10-22, before the people audits: no new statements are added.

missingStatements.text: Problems in personal and family life between women and men are political problems that require collective rather than individual solutions.
missingStatements.rationale: Hanisch's 'the personal is political' and the Redstockings Manifesto's claim that every male-female relationship is a class relationship are foundational radical feminist positions.
missingStatements.declined: Statement bank frozen on 2026-10-22, before the people audits: no new statements are added.

notes: Answers on pornography law, gender identity, women's distinct values, reproductive technology and the relation of women and nature are neutral or low because radical feminists themselves divide on them. Many economic and foreign-policy statements are untouched by the primary texts and are answered neutral or low; radical feminists generally came from the New Left but subordinated economic class to sex-class.
